name: loom-runtime
description: loom's runtime piece: boxes and houses, model accounts, harness runners, model choice and delivery

loom.name: runtime
loom.label: Runtime
loom.description: The runtime: the machines (boxes) and containers (houses) agents run in, their model accounts, the harnesses that run a body, which model it runs on, and delivery: anything addressed to an agent becomes a body handling it.

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_LOOM_URL
settings.label: loom's MCP URL, as this machine reaches it

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_PUBLIC_URL
settings.label: loom's URL for other boxes
settings.hint: what a new box joins, e.g. https://loom.example.com

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_ACCOUNTS
settings.label: Model accounts
settings.hint: unset: the accounts the boxes' logins report (docs/model-accounts.md); none: don't read quota

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE
settings.label: A runtime token, for core's conversation records and scorecards
settings.hint: a file holding a token with loom's runtime role; without one, delivery writes no turns (and answers 503) and model choice reads no scorecards

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_BUSY_LIMIT
settings.label: Bodies an agent has mid-turn before a new conversation waits

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_SPAWN_LIMIT
settings.label: Spawned jobs an agent has running before a new one waits
settings.hint: 1-32; a body whose house is draining, stopping or gone doesn't count

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_SEAT_HOUSES
settings.label: Houses an agent may have at once for anyone but its owner

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_WARM_IDLE_S
settings.label: Seconds a body whose turn is over stays warm

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_CONTINUITY
settings.label: How long a conversation's slot is kept, in days
settings.hint: JSON by venue or venue kind, e.g. {"slack": 7, "scheduled": 1}; at most 14 (default live 14, scheduled 1, agent 3)

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_RETRY_S
settings.label: How long a body that couldn't start waits before each new try
settings.hint: a JSON list of seconds, 1-5 of them (default [60, 240, 600]: about 15 minutes); after the last, it's given up and the owner is told

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_BODY_ENV
settings.label: More of the runtime's environment a body may have
settings.hint: variable names, comma-separated; never LOOM_*, a harness's settings or a provider's key (a body in a house runs in the house's own environment)

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_GRADER_IMAGE
settings.label: The review's grader image, pinned by digest
settings.hint: name@sha256:…, built from grader/Containerfile on loom's machine; without it the review grades nothing (never in an agent's house image)

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_REVIEW_LIMIT
settings.label: Audit entries the daily review grades, at most
settings.hint: 1-2000; the review runs at 04:00 in the household's time zone (household.json tz and review, read from core)

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_REVIEW_INTROSPECT
settings.label: Which agents review their own day after grading
settings.hint: all (every agent the runtime hosts), none, or agent ids, comma-separated; each runs as itself, in its own house

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_NOW_DIR
settings.label: Where the now board's files are
settings.hint: a directory: each agent's board in <agent>-now under it (the bridges' snapshots and events, no message text); default the runtime's own data

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_BRIDGE_DARK_S
settings.label: Seconds a bridge may be silent, with nothing to explain it, before it's down
settings.hint: 30 to 86400; a bridge the runtime is restarting is never down for it, and one that keeps restarting is an alert at once

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_RELAY_HEADS_UP
settings.label: A relay thread this long is a heads-up
settings.hint: messages in one thread within a day, on loom's Inbox (default 8); never a stop

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_LOCAL_BODIES
settings.label: Agents whose local wakes have their bodies on this machine
settings.hint: JSON {"agents":["art"],"cwd":"/home/art/Art",...}; also codex, machineClaudeLogin; house:["local-lane:plan"] or where:"house" runs those in the owner's house; unset: refused

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_ALERT_COMMAND
settings.label: The owner's alert command
settings.hint: a JSON argv; gets <source> --severity --summary --fact k=v for what the runtime notices (bridge down, loop pause, failed start), detached

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_STUCK_AFTER
settings.label: Minutes a body on loom's machine may wait on a permission prompt
settings.hint: then it's stopped (its session kept), noted on its task and said once; 0 or off: never

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_TASK_COMMENT
settings.label: How a stopped stuck body is noted on its task
settings.hint: a JSON argv with {task} and {text}; unset: taskstore comment {task} {text} when taskstore is on the local bodies' PATH; off: never

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_CONTINUATION_DAYS
settings.label: Days a follow-up report capability lasts
settings.hint: 1-13; a wake can carry it until then, and nothing renews it. Anything else stops new ones

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_CONTINUATION_KEEP_DAYS
settings.label: Days finished follow-up reports are kept after their deadline

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_HOST_RULES
settings.label: Ask the owner's standing rules for steps on loom's machine

options.label: No: each step runs at its own tier
Yes: the owner's rule on the Approvals page decides

settings.hint: needs the approvals piece with host rules (t-2104); an unreadable answer is the step's own tier

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_JOB_PROFILES
settings.label: Job profile declarations
settings.hint: Runtime-owned JSON store path. Claude jobs with missing or invalid declarations select no MCP, tools, skills or secrets and a visible problem; no off override. Codex jobs without a matching declaration retain their existing environment and brief; declared Codex profiles fail closed.

settings.name: LOOM_RUNTIME_CONTEXT_CAP
settings.label: Job context before a fresh session handoff
settings.hint: Scheduled and spawned jobs only; 20000–2000000 tokens; off disables. Cooperative handoff at a safe tool boundary; see docs/context-continuation.md.

relay.description: Ask another agent in this household something: it reaches a body of theirs with your words, framed as a peer's request (none of the owner's authority). Include conversation to return answers to your requesting session. Without asking only between agents the household pairs (the runtime's permissions); for any other, ask the owner first (approvals request --kind relay --target <you>-><them>) and pass the allowed approval. The same words twice within the hour are refused. Answer a relay with reply_to set to its id.

say.description: What to tell or ask them (8000 characters at most; point at a PR or file for more)

why.description: One line: why you are asking

from.description: Where it was asked, e.g. "discord:#workshop", so the answer can go back there

approval.description: An approval id (a-…) the owner allowed, for a relay the household doesn't pair

conversation.description: Your current conversation (cv-…): replies resume it, or its saved session, as peer messages

comms_trace.description: What happened to a reply of yours, from the message in to the reply shown: delivered to you, your body started and ended, what you sent and what was refused, whether the venue took it and whether the thread shows it. Name a Comms thread (th:…), a run (run-…) or a conversation (cv-…) of your own; never another agent's. No words, only what happened.

thread.description: A Comms thread of yours, th:…

run.description: A run of yours, run-… (its steps; else the newest run's)

spawn.description: Hand an independent job to a fresh body of yourself: it runs with its own model, account and lifecycle, and its final report returns here. Principal and house rules carry over. action roles lists the kinds of work you can ask for (they change: read them, don't assume); pass role to have the runtime pick the model, and the job keeps that model on every resume. action say steers it, result fetches its report. Work inside your own job (a few parallel lookups or edits) can still use your harness's own subagents: they share your job's model and account. If the asking conversation is ambiguous, use loom runtime spawn from your shell.

action.description: start (default), say, result, or roles (the work roles you can ask for)

role.description: A work role from action roles; the runtime picks an eligible model

failover.description: Allow the job to move to another eligible model if its own runs out of quota (default: it waits)

handle.description: Handle from start, for say or result
